text: Chronic intermittent hypobaric hypoxia (4300 m; 450 Torr; 10 weeks) altered the NMDA receptor in 3-week-old rats. In cerebral cortex, hippocampus and corpus striatum, [3H]MK-801 binding showed reduced Bmax (36%, 35%, 31%) and decreased Kd (29%, 32%, 17%) versus normoxic controls, indicating increased affinity. In cortex, glutamate (100 µM) and glycine (10 µM) enhanced binding two- to threefold. Glutamate EC50 was higher in hypoxic membranes (0.44 µM) than in controls (0.28 µM); glycine EC50 did not differ significantly. The NMDA receptor is altered in several brain regions of rats developing in a hypoxic environment.
